items.title: Browser Probe: let Claude actually look at your web app
items.summary: Claude drives a real headless Chrome so it can screenshot every screen of your web app, catch JavaScript errors, and spot bugs that only show up on screen. No Playwright or Puppeteer needed.
items.how_to_use: Ask Claude: "test the UI", "screenshot every screen at phone size" or "it looks wrong but the data is fine, find out why".
items.requires: Google Chrome and Node 22 or newer.
items.install_prompt:
Please install the Claude Code skill "Browser Probe: let Claude actually look at your web app" from my friend's Claude Shelf.
1. Download https://jesse372.github.io/claude-shelf/items/browser-probe/browser-probe.zip
2. Unzip it into ~/.claude/skills/ so it ends up at ~/.claude/skills/browser-probe/SKILL.md
3. Read the files first and tell me if anything looks risky, needs an API key, or costs money. Ask me before installing anything system-wide.
4. Set up anything SKILL.md says it needs, then tell me in plain words how to use it.

items.title: Voice: Claude talks and listens
items.summary: Free text-to-speech with natural Microsoft neural voices (falls back to the Mac's built-in voice offline), plus offline transcription of voice notes and recordings with Whisper.
items.how_to_use: Say "read it to me", "say that out loud", or "transcribe this voice note".
items.requires: macOS. pip install edge-tts for the good voices; whisper.cpp or openai-whisper for transcription.

items.title: LLM Council
items.summary: Put a big decision in front of 5 AI advisors who each think differently. They review each other's answers anonymously, then a chairman gives you one verdict showing where they agree and where they clash.
items.how_to_use: Say to Claude: "council this: should I do X or Y?" and give it real context (numbers, stakes, constraints). Best for decisions where being wrong is expensive.
items.requires: Claude Code. No API keys by default (it uses Claude sub-agents). Optional multi-model mode with your own keys.

items.title: Memory Capture: Claude remembers past sessions
items.summary: Automatically turns finished Claude Code (and Codex) sessions into short, durable decision notes, so later you can ask 'what did we decide about X?' and get an answer.
items.how_to_use: Install it, then ask "what did we decide about…", "have we done this before?" or "search memory for…".
items.requires: Claude Code. Originally set up with a ~/JesseOS/vault folder; tell Claude where you want your notes kept.

items.title: Pipeline QC: automations that fix themselves
items.summary: A framework that checks every stage of a recurring automation and repairs failures itself. It does a simple fix first, then lets Claude attempt a repair (kept only if the check goes green), and only pings you if both fail.
items.how_to_use: Ask Claude: "add a self-healing QC loop to this pipeline" or "make this workflow monitor itself". It wires your stages into qc-lib.sh.
items.requires: macOS/Linux bash and Claude Code. Notifications are pluggable (desktop by default).

items.title: Web Essentials: favicon + iPhone home-screen icon
items.summary: A checklist Claude follows on every website it builds: a favicon, a proper iPhone Add-to-Home-Screen icon, and the right meta tags. Includes a script that turns any emoji into all the icons in one command.
items.how_to_use: It kicks in whenever you ask Claude to build a web page. Or run: python3 ~/.claude/skills/web-essentials/scripts/emoji_icon.py "🚀" --title "My Site"
items.requires: macOS (Apple emoji font) and Python with Pillow (pip install pillow).

items.title: Wrap-up: the end-of-project checklist
items.summary: Before Claude calls anything 'done', it checks for things that will break silently later (expired logins, jobs that stopped running, untested cron paths), hardens them, saves reusable skills and writes notes to memory.
items.how_to_use: Say "wrap up" or "is this done?" at the end of any project. You can also run scripts/audit.sh for a quick inventory.
items.requires: Claude Code. Most useful on macOS with LaunchAgents/cron jobs.
